builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Cognitive Agentic AI Framework for Interactive Process Analysis and Optimization
summary: It replaces manual, iterative coordination across disconnected simulation, database, retrieval, and optimization tools with an LLM that interprets prompts, plans, and delegates numerical work to specialized providers under a fixed process topology. Costs are LLM inference calls across long interactive sessions (4,000 BO iterations in the demo), integration effort to build and maintain the tool providers, and dependence on an external simulator such as COCO. It can fail through non-converged simulations, invalid tool outputs, or ML-surrogate predictions that diverge from simulator ground truth outside explored operating bounds, which is why human-guided verification remains necessary.
rationale: The pattern (LLM handles interpretation and planning while deterministic tools handle numerics) is replicable with a single GPU or API access, but the reported gains are specific to chemical process optimization with a COCO simulation stack, so adoption value depends on having analogous domain tools and data.
technique: LLM agent harness orchestrating engineering tools

claims.statement: It replaces manual, iterative coordination across disconnected simulation, database, retrieval, and optimization tools with an LLM that interprets prompts, plans, and delegates numerical work to specialized providers under a fixed process topology. Costs are LLM inference calls across long interactive sessions (4,000 BO iterations in the demo), integration effort to build and maintain the tool providers, and dependence on an external simulator such as COCO. It can fail through non-converged simulations, invalid tool outputs, or ML-surrogate predictions that diverge from simulator ground truth outside explored operating bounds, which is why human-guided verification remains necessary.

BO-guided exploration verified by COCO simulation raised carbon conversion yield from approximately 0.81 to 0.921 (about 11 percentage points), with re-simulation of 16 candidates showing a mean absolute C-Yield error of 0.0085 against ML predictions.
